title: CurveToMeshNode — sweep profile along curve path
description: Implement a curve_to_mesh DSL node equivalent to Blender's GeometryNodeCurveToMesh. Converts a curve into a mesh by sweeping a profile curve along the path curve. If no profile is provided, creates a simple ribbon/strip mesh along the curve. This enables pipe/tube generation, edge-to-cylinder conversion, and decorative trim creation. Reference: Blender-Procedural-Human pipes.py utility uses this for cylindrical pipe generation from mesh edges. Note: CurveSweepMeshNode already exists but requires an explicit mesh profile face — this node should accept a curve profile or default to a circle.
definition-of-done:
1. New CurveToMeshNode class in ixdar-app/src/main/java/ixdar/geometry/mesh/nodes/curve/ with @MeshNodeAnnotation id 'curve_to_mesh'
2. Input ports: curve (GeometryBundleValue — curve data), profile_curve (optional GeometryBundleValue — profile shape), fill_caps (BooleanField, default=true), resolution (IntField, default=12 — circle resolution when no profile given)
3. Output port: geometry (MeshValue) — the generated tube/sweep mesh
4. When no profile_curve: generate a circular cross-section with given resolution
5. When profile_curve provided: use it as the sweep cross-section
6. Sweep maintains parallel transport frame along path (like existing CurveSweepMeshNode)
7. Registered in MeshNodeRegistry and usable in .dsl files
testing-plan:
1. Unit test: curve_to_mesh on a straight line curve — verify cylinder-like output with expected vertex count
2. Unit test: curve_to_mesh with circular profile — verify tube mesh topology
3. Unit test: curve_to_mesh with fill_caps=true vs false — verify cap faces present/absent
4. DSL integration: create a grid, mesh_to_curve, curve_to_mesh — verify pipe mesh
5. Mesh probe: verify bounding box matches expected dimensions
